# Geometry Fundamentals

[Point → Line → Edge → Face → Solid → Boolean]({{ site.baseurl }}/sessions/#b03) · Target weeks 4–5

Build geometry from coordinates, then use the parametric pyramid as a Boolean cutter.

Use these example files only as a reference if you are struggling with a step. Build your own file and follow the process one step at a time. Compare the example to understand where you are stuck, then return to your own work. The supplied examples are not files to submit as your assignment.

Select the lesson object and change parameters on the nodes or, where provided, in the GeometryNodes modifier. Press Home over the node editor. Explanations are in Frames and native node names are retained. Build the exercise in a new file of your own, following each step in order.

## Example files and steps

**[Geometry Fundamentals]({{ site.baseurl }}/files/blender/02-geometry-fundamentals/GEOMETRY101-class-ready.blend)**

1. Point
2. Line
3. Edge
4. Face
5. Solid
6. Boolean

Follow the six main teaching scenes. Original reference scenes remain in the file. The pyramid keeps Width, Depth and Height exposed and the file ends with cube-minus-pyramid. This is a model-units lesson, not a fabrication export.

## Short assignment

Show a point, line, edge, face, solid pyramid and cube-minus-pyramid result. Keep Width, Depth and Height exposed; include a mesh with multiple faces.

## Lesson notes and project connection

[Geometry from scratch]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/tutorials/u03-geometry-from-scratch/) — The panel you build here is the component P2 arrays and the object P1c prints. The parameters you expose now are the ones an attractor drives in P2b, so choose numbers worth varying.

Develop this exercise in [P1 — Geometry — from operations to construction]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/assignments/p1-geometry-from-operations-to-construction/).
